subject: Renewal + mid-contract capacity add — pricing alignment and one-off concession
messages:
From: Jessie Carroll <jessie.carroll@luminex.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@luminex.com
Date: 2026-10-09T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Renewal conversation + extra capacity request

Hi Sofia,

Hope you’re well — our fiscal Q1 planning landed a month earlier than expected and we’re looking to lock in an expanded commit with Redwood as part of our renewal. Current contract with Redwood ends 2027-01-31. Two quick asks:

- We need +30% committed capacity starting 2026-11-01 for a new pilot (expected to sustain).
- We’d like to co-term the additional capacity to our existing renewal date rather than a separate 12-month add-on.

We’ve loved the reliability, but procurement is pushing to consolidate pricing — asking if there’s room for a one-time uplift concession or a blended-rate for the remainder of this term. Attaching the SOW for the new pilot.

Can we get a proposal by EOD Tuesday?

Thanks,
Jessie Carroll
Sr. Manager, Platform Integrations
Luminex

Attachment: Luminex_SOW_v3.pdf (pdf)
From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.com>
To: Jessie Carroll <jessie.carroll@luminex.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, procurement@luminex.com
Date: 2026-10-09T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal conversation + extra capacity request

Hi Jessie — thanks for the heads-up and for sending the SOW.

We can absolutely support the +30% capacity and co-term to 2027-01-31. To make that work commercially, I want to be transparent about two levers we normally use: blended-rate (prorated across the remaining term) or a short-term uplift credit (one-time credit to offset unit pricing). I’ve looped in Ben (AE) and Kimberly (Sales Ops) to align on discounting guardrails and approval path.

Ben/Kimberly — can you confirm a quick proposal we can commit to by Tuesday? If possible, include a blended-rate example and a one-time concession so Jessie can review with procurement. I’ve attached the SOW so legal/procurement have the scope.

Sofia Ivanova
Head of Strategic Accounts — Redwood Inference
sofia.ivanova@redwood.com
+1 415-555-0123

Attachment: Luminex_SOW_v3.pdf (re-sent)
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-09T13:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal conversation + extra capacity request (internal)

Sofia — thanks. Quick notes after an initial look at the SOW: expected steady-state token consumption will likely justify keeping Luminex on our current M-tier model, but the pilot front-loads throughput for three months.

Options we can present:
1) Blended prorated rate: 30% capacity added immediately, prorate the unit price across remaining 3.75 months so their effective unit price is ~7% lower than a straight top-up.
2) One-time uplift credit: give a $30k credit applied to the next invoice if they commit to the co-term and sign an amendment by Oct 20.
3) Hybrid: smaller credit ($15k) + modest blended discount (~3%).

Approval cushion: Kim, what’s the max exec-level concession we can offer without further escalations? Also need to validate whether Finance will accept the credit accounting for a midterm term-end prune.

Ben
Account Executive — Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-09T14:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal conversation + extra capacity request (internal)

Ben — Finance will greenlight a credit up to $35k on a one-off basis if the deal structure preserves ARR visibility (i.e., we annualize the additional committed capacity for reporting but co-term billing remains to 2027-01-31).

Notes for the customer-facing proposal:
- Present both blended-rate and credit options side-by-side with clear cashflow impact across the remainder of the term.
- Call out that longer-term expansion (12+ months beyond renewal) can qualify for a volume band that lowers unit price beyond these one-off options.

If Ben can draft the customer email today, I’ll sign off and attach a finance-approved quote template.

Kimberly Park
Sales Operations Manager — Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwood.com
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Jessie Carroll <jessie.carroll@luminex.com>
Cc: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, procurement@luminex.com
Date: 2026-10-10T09:30:00-07:00
Subject: Proposed options for Luminex mid-term addition and co-terming

Hi Jessie — appreciate the quick turnaround. Based on SOW scope, we put together two straightforward options for the +30% capacity starting 2026-11-01, co-terming to your existing 2027-01-31 renewal date. See attached quote (Luminex_Renewal_Quote_Q4.xlsx).

Option A — Blended prorated rate
- 30% additional committed units applied 2026-11-01 through 2027-01-31
- Effective blended unit price across remainder of term: $0.0117/token (~7% reduction vs straight top-up)
- No upfront credits; billing prorated over remaining invoices

Option B — One-time concession credit + standard rate
- No change in per-unit list rate; we apply a one-time $30,000 credit on your next invoice if amendment signed by Oct 20
- Credit absorbs much of the uplift cost during the pilot months and keeps unit economics simple for procurement

Hybrid — $15k credit + ~3% blended reduction (also available if you prefer middle ground).

Next steps: let me know which option you prefer and I’ll generate the amendment for signature. If procurement wants additional visibility into monthly invoice impact, we can include a simple amortization table.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Account Executive — Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com
+1 628-555-0199

Attachment: Luminex_Renewal_Quote_Q4.xlsx (Excel)
From: Jessie Carroll <jessie.carroll@luminex.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@luminex.com, Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-12T16:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Proposed options for Luminex mid-term addition and co-terming

Ben/Kim/Sofia — thanks for the quick proposal. Procurement prefers Option A (blended prorated rate) because it keeps accounting cleaner for our Q1 close. Two small asks before we sign:

1) Can you confirm the monthly invoice delta in USD for Nov/Dec/Jan so our finance team can model cashflow?
2) If we expand further at renewal, will the blended portion be eligible to roll into any volume band pricing? (we may add another +40% at renewal)

If you can send a one-page amortization table for the three months and a short note on eligibility for volume banding, we’ll aim to sign the amendment by Oct 18.

Best,
Jessie Carroll
Sr. Manager, Platform Integrations — Luminex
procurement@luminex.com
